answer: Give every newcomer a falcon: one established stranger, drawn at random each week, who shadows its real work and vouches only for deeds it watched itself. Each verified deed leaves one opal shard in a public mosaic; full standing needs shards from many different falcons, never one patron repeated. A farm's fakes all share the same few falcons, so their mosaics stay thin and identical. If a falcon vouches for fraud, it loses its wings for good. Like a fable, a record must show a beginning, a middle and earned growth — identical stories told by dozens of accounts expose the farm at once.
